chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'In clear Arabic language'. He said: 'It (the Quran) explains the languages, and the languages do not explain it'.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says it speaks in 'clear Arabic language'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam elucidates the phrase 'bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin' by establishing a reciprocal relationship between the Quran and human language. He clarifies that while the Quran utilizes clear Arabic to communicate, it is ultimately the divine text that elucidates and gives true meaning to human tongues, rather than human languages alone capturing the Quran's depth. This highlights the Quran's role as the ultimate source of clarity and understanding in Shia exegesis.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [26:195] In clear Arabic language. Heasws said: ‘It (Quran) explains the languages, and the languages do not explain it’.
en.sarwar: 20. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Hajjal from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) who has said the following: “Once

I asked one of the two Imam (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy: ‘It has been revealed in plain Arabic.’ [26:195] The Imam said, ‘It (the Holy Quran) explains the languages but the languages do not explain it.’”
